items.title: Hospital pharmacy short-shipped after phosphate binder supplier slip
items.body: A contract manufacturer pushed back two consecutive dispatches of a phosphate binder SKU. The hospital pharmacy at Fictiva General received partial deliveries for several weeks. The issue surfaced through repeated ETA revisions rather than through the account itself. We learned to watch ETA slips as an early warning before fill rate visibly drops.

steps.action: Split available stock pro rata across affected hospital accounts
Escalate to supplier and obtain a committed dispatch date
Share the revised ETA with the pharmacy purchase lead

items.resolution: Split remaining stock across hospital accounts pro rata, escalate supplier, share revised ETA with pharmacy

items.title: Chemist chain switched source during prolonged supplier delay
items.body: An active ingredient shortage at an upstream supplier delayed a chronic CKD SKU for over a month. The Kestrel Pharmacies chain was not contacted until its orders had already stopped. By the time stock returned, the chain had moved the line to an alternative source. The lesson was that silence during a delay costs more than the delay itself.

steps.action: Restore supply once supplier dispatch arrived
Visit the chain buyer to request reinstatement of the line

items.resolution: Late outreach after stock returned; no interim supply offered

items.title: Nephrology clinic orders paused during iron supplement supplier delay
items.body: A packaging line breakdown at a supplier delayed an oral iron supplement SKU. The Riverbend Kidney Clinic paused orders and logged a delivery complaint. Operations noticed the low stock cover at the regional warehouse a few days late. Supply recovered, but the clinic reduced its standing order for the following quarter.

steps.action: Escalate supplier and confirm repair timeline
Release part of the regional buffer to the clinic
Call the clinic with the revised ETA

items.resolution: Escalate supplier, contact clinic with revised ETA, partial reallocation from regional buffer

items.title: Stockist ran dry on a high-velocity renal SKU before month-end
items.body: A regional stockist under-ordered ahead of a holiday period and ran out of a high-velocity SKU. Downstream chemists began reporting unavailability through field reps. Our warehouse had stock; the gap was in the channel, not upstream. An expedited replenishment closed the gap within days.

steps.action: Raise an expedited dispatch from the nearest warehouse
Agree a minimum holding norm with the stockist
Inform field reps that stock is restored

items.resolution: Expedite replenishment from warehouse, agree a minimum stock norm with the stockist

items.title: Chemist chain outlets out of stock after central DC transfer delay
items.body: The Northgate Chemists central distribution centre delayed inter-store transfers during a system migration. Several outlets showed empty shelves while the chain's central stock was healthy. We noticed via a dip in outlet-level orders routed through the stockist. Direct-to-outlet dispatch for a short window bridged the gap.

steps.action: Identify affected outlets with the chain logistics lead
Arrange temporary direct dispatch to those outlets
Confirm normal transfers resumed before stopping direct dispatch

items.resolution: Temporary direct dispatch to affected outlets, coordinate with chain logistics

items.title: Hospital pharmacy stockout from missed tender call-off
items.body: The hospital pharmacy at Lakeview Medical Centre missed a scheduled call-off under its annual tender. Pharmacy stock ran low before anyone on either side noticed. The reorder interval had been drifting for weeks, which was the earliest sign. The account was recovered but the procurement relationship was strained.

steps.action: Process an emergency call-off against the tender
Agree a reorder reminder cadence with hospital procurement

items.resolution: Emergency call-off processed, reorder reminder cadence agreed with procurement

items.title: Warehouse system showed stock that was physically unavailable
items.body: Orders from a stockist were confirmed against system stock that turned out to be quarantined. Dispatches were short and the stockist was given inaccurate ETAs. A cycle count revealed the quarantine flag had not synced to the order system. The sync rule was fixed and the stockist was given priority dispatch.

steps.action: Run a cycle count on the affected SKU locations
Correct the quarantine status sync with the IT team
Give the stockist a corrected ETA and priority dispatch

items.resolution: Cycle count, fix quarantine sync, priority dispatch to affected stockist

items.title: Near-expiry stock stranded at one depot while another ran short
items.body: One depot held a large lot approaching expiry while a neighbouring depot could not fill chain orders. The imbalance was visible only when expiry exposure was reviewed at month-end. A redistribution moved usable stock to where demand was before the expiry window closed. We now review expiry exposure alongside cover days rather than separately.

steps.action: Identify lots within the redistribution window
Transfer usable lots to the short depot
Confirm acceptance terms with the chain buyer

items.resolution: Redistribute near-expiry stock to the short depot within the usable window

items.title: Nephrology clinic received wrong pack size after master data error
items.body: A pack size mapping error in item master data caused the Hillcrest Renal Clinic to receive the wrong presentation. The clinic raised a delivery complaint and returned the consignment. The error affected only one SKU code and was traced within a few days. The correct stock was dispatched and the mapping was locked behind a review step.

steps.action: Correct the pack size mapping in item master
Arrange return and replacement consignment
Close the complaint with the clinic

items.resolution: Correct item master mapping, replace consignment, add review step for master data edits

items.title: Cluster of packaging complaints on one batch from a stockist region
items.body: Several chemists served by one stockist reported damaged blister packs from the same batch. The complaints clustered on a single batch code within a short period. The cluster was routed to the QA head, who placed the batch on hold pending investigation. Commercial teams made no product statements and directed all queries to QA.

steps.action: Classify complaints and link them to the batch code
Preserve complaint records and retained samples
Route the cluster to the QA head for four-eyes review
Record the QA batch hold decision and notify operations

items.resolution: Route to QA head, four-eyes review of the cluster, batch hold decision by QA

items.title: Hospital pharmacy reported a visual defect in one batch
items.body: The pharmacy at Fictiva General reported a visual defect in tablets from one batch. One report was flagged as a suspected adverse event and was routed separately to the safety process. The QA head ran a four-eyes review and decided on a precautionary batch hold. The account was kept informed of process status only, with no product or clinical commentary from commercial staff.

steps.action: Classify the report and separate the suspected adverse event
Preserve evidence and batch documentation
Route to the QA head for four-eyes review
Record the QA batch hold decision

items.resolution: Route to QA head, four-eyes review, batch hold decision by QA; suspected AE routed to safety process

items.title: Slow QA routing on a chemist chain batch complaint
items.body: Outlets in the Kestrel Pharmacies chain reported label legibility issues on one batch. The complaints sat in the general support queue before being recognised as a cluster. Once routed, the QA head completed a four-eyes review and recorded a batch decision. The delay frustrated the chain and it reduced orders for a period.

steps.action: Classify the complaints as a batch cluster
Route to the QA head for four-eyes review
Record the QA decision and inform the account of process status

items.resolution: Route to QA head, four-eyes review, batch hold decision by QA; add cluster auto-routing

items.title: Territory vacancy left nephrology clinics unvisited
items.body: A rep resignation left a territory uncovered for several weeks. Visit gaps grew at nephrology clinics and orders softened in parallel. Coverage was restored by assigning a neighbouring rep until the vacancy was filled. Most accounts recovered once visits resumed.

steps.action: Assign interim cover from a neighbouring territory
Prioritise visits to the highest-value clinics
Introduce the interim rep to clinic contacts

items.resolution: Assign neighbouring rep as interim cover, prioritise high-value clinics

items.title: Hospital pharmacy relationship lapsed during long rep absence
items.body: A long-term rep absence was not backfilled at the Lakeview Medical Centre pharmacy. Formulary review meetings were missed and a competing product gained position. The gap was noticed only when the next tender cycle opened. We learned that hospital accounts need named backup coverage, not best-effort visits.

steps.action: Assign a named backup rep for the account
Request a meeting with pharmacy procurement

items.resolution: Late reassignment of coverage after tender cycle opened

items.title: Stockist orders dipped after rep focus shifted to new launch
items.body: Reps were redirected to a new product launch and routine stockist calls dropped off. Order volumes at mid-sized stockists softened over the following weeks. A rebalanced call plan restored routine contact without pausing the launch. Orders recovered within a cycle.

steps.action: Rebalance the call plan across launch and routine accounts
Schedule catch-up calls with affected stockists

items.resolution: Rebalance call plan to restore routine stockist contact

items.title: Stockist under credit strain stretched reorder intervals
items.body: A stockist's overdue receivables rose and its reorder intervals stretched. Finance flagged the account before a credit hold was triggered automatically. A structured payment plan kept supply flowing while the overdue balance came down. The account normalised over the following quarter.

steps.action: Review receivables and credit exposure
Agree a payment plan with the stockist
Adjust order release to the reduced credit limit

items.resolution: Agree a payment plan with finance, keep supply on reduced credit limit

items.title: Stockist orders fell after CKD-MBD binder supplier slip
items.body: A supplier delay on a CKD-MBD phosphate binder SKU left the Meridian Distributors stockist short for several weeks. Fill rate dropped, the stockist's orders fell for about a month, and delivery complaints piled up while support responses slowed. The pattern was noticed when repeated ETA slips coincided with falling warehouse stock cover and fewer rep interactions. Operations reallocated inventory from lower-priority accounts and escalated the supplier, and the account manager called the stockist to agree interim supply. The stockist stayed with us; the lesson was that early, proactive contact during a supplier slip protects the relationship.

steps.action: Reallocate stock of the delayed SKU from lower-priority accounts to the affected stockist
Escalate to the supplier and obtain a revised, committed ETA
Call the stockist, share the revised ETA and agree interim supply quantities
Follow up on the stockist's open delivery complaints until closed

items.resolution: Reallocate inventory from lower-priority accounts, escalate supplier, contact customer

items.title: Chemist chain payment delays after its own funding squeeze
items.body: The Northgate Chemists chain delayed payments across suppliers during a funding squeeze. Our receivables aged and the chain cut order value to essentials. A credit hold was placed after negotiations stalled, and the chain moved volume elsewhere. The overdue balance was eventually recovered, but the commercial relationship did not recover.

steps.action: Escalate overdue balance to finance and business head
Place the account on credit hold
Negotiate recovery of the overdue balance

items.resolution: Credit hold after stalled payment negotiation

items.title: Nephrology clinic billing dispute held up payments
items.body: The Riverbend Kidney Clinic withheld payment over a disputed invoice. Overdue receivables grew and a billing complaint was logged. The dispute was traced to a duplicated credit note and corrected. Payments resumed once the corrected statement was shared.

steps.action: Reconcile the disputed invoice and credit notes
Share the corrected statement with the clinic
Close the billing complaint

items.resolution: Reconcile disputed invoice, issue corrected statement, resume normal terms

items.title: Regional support backlog after seasonal ticket surge
items.body: A post-holiday surge in delivery queries overwhelmed one regional support desk. Response times stretched and stockists began escalating through field reps. Tickets were rebalanced to another region's desk and a triage rule was introduced. The backlog cleared within about a week.

steps.action: Move overflow tickets to a less loaded regional desk
Introduce a triage rule prioritising stockist delivery queries
Brief field reps on the expected response window

items.resolution: Rebalance tickets across regional desks, introduce triage rule

items.title: Hospital pharmacy escalated over unanswered queries
items.body: Two support staff were on leave at once and hospital queries went unanswered for days. The pharmacy at Fictiva General escalated to the business head. A named support contact was assigned to hospital accounts from then on. The account accepted the fix after a review call.

steps.action: Assign a named support contact for hospital accounts
Hold a review call with the pharmacy
Add a leave-overlap check to support rostering

items.resolution: Assign named support contact for hospital accounts, cover leave overlaps

items.title: Chemist chain complaints aged during support tool migration
items.body: A support tool migration left some chain complaints invisible in the new queue. Response times rose sharply for the Kestrel Pharmacies chain. Missing tickets were recovered from the old system and worked down by a temporary squad. The chain remained a customer but asked for a monthly service review.

steps.action: Recover tickets missing from the new queue
Stand up a temporary squad to clear the backlog
Set up a monthly service review with the chain

items.resolution: Recover missing tickets, temporary squad to clear backlog, monthly service review

items.title: Nephrology clinic growth opened a cross-sell for an adjacent CKD SKU
items.body: The Hillcrest Renal Clinic expanded its dialysis unit and its orders for our binder SKU grew steadily. The rep noticed that the clinic sourced an adjacent CKD SKU from elsewhere. A cross-sell visit with approved product information and supply terms added the SKU to the clinic's orders. The growth held over the following quarters.

steps.action: Plan a cross-sell visit with approved product information materials
Agree supply terms for the adjacent SKU
Confirm stock cover for the added volume

items.resolution: Cross-sell visit for adjacent SKU, align supply terms

items.title: Stockist demand rose in a new catchment, cross-sell landed
items.body: A new dialysis centre opened in the Meridian Distributors catchment and stockist orders rose. The account manager proposed adding two adjacent renal SKUs to the stockist's range. Operations confirmed supply before the offer was made. The stockist took both lines and order value grew.

steps.action: Confirm warehouse cover for the proposed SKUs
Present the range extension to the stockist
Track uptake over the next two order cycles

items.resolution: Cross-sell adjacent renal SKUs after confirming supply

items.title: Supplier delay on a chronic SKU
items.body: Use when a supplier ETA slips on a chronic-therapy SKU and downstream accounts start to run short. The aim is to protect continuity for the most exposed accounts, get a firm date from the supplier and tell customers early. Proactive customer contact is the step most often skipped and the one past incidents show matters most.

steps.action: Check warehouse stock cover and inbound ETA for the SKU
Reallocate inventory from lower-priority accounts to the most exposed accounts
Escalate to the supplier and obtain a revised, committed ETA
Contact each affected customer, share the revised ETA and agree interim supply
Follow up on open delivery complaints from affected accounts
Monitor fill rate and order volume for affected accounts until supply normalises

items.title: Batch complaint triage
items.body: Use when two or more quality complaints reference the same batch code within a short window. Commercial and support staff classify, preserve and route only; every batch disposition decision belongs to the QA head under four-eyes review. No product, clinical or patient-facing statements are made by anyone outside QA.

steps.action: Classify the complaints as a possible batch cluster and link each to its batch code
Preserve complaint records, photos and any returned packs as evidence
Route the cluster to the QA head with the evidence pack
QA head and second QA reviewer complete a four-eyes review of the cluster
Record the QA batch decision (hold, release or investigate) and notify operations

items.title: Near-expiry stock redistribution
items.body: Use when expiry exposure at one location is high while another location or account is short on the same SKU. Move usable lots to where demand exists while they are still within the acceptable remaining shelf-life window. Never offer stock outside the agreed shelf-life terms.

steps.action: List lots approaching the redistribution cut-off by location
Match lots to locations or accounts short on the same SKU
Confirm shelf-life acceptance terms with receiving accounts
Execute inter-location transfers
Review residual expiry exposure and record write-off candidates

items.title: Credit hold and payment plan
items.body: Use when an account's overdue receivables cross the credit policy threshold or reorder intervals stretch alongside ageing dues. Prefer a structured payment plan that keeps supply flowing over an outright hold, unless the business head decides otherwise. A credit hold is a business decision, not an automated one.

steps.action: Review receivables ageing and current credit exposure
Contact the account to understand the cause of delay
Propose a payment plan with a reduced credit limit
Decide on payment plan or credit hold
Apply the decided order release rule in operations

items.title: Rep-vacancy territory cover
items.body: Use when a territory loses its rep or rep coverage falls well below plan. Assign named interim cover immediately and prioritise accounts by value and visit gap. Hospital accounts always get a named backup, not best-effort visits.

steps.action: Confirm the vacancy and list accounts in the territory by value and visit gap
Assign named interim cover from a neighbouring territory
Introduce the interim rep to key account contacts
Schedule visits to accounts with the largest visit gaps first
Monitor interaction frequency and orders until the vacancy is filled

items.title: Support surge handling
items.body: Use when response times or the regional support backlog rise well above normal. Rebalance work across desks, triage by account risk and keep field teams informed of expected response windows.

steps.action: Check backlog and response times by region and queue
Move overflow tickets to less loaded desks
Apply triage priority to at-risk accounts and quality-related tickets
Brief field reps and account managers on expected response windows
Review staffing and rostering once the backlog clears

items.title: Cross-sell visit on demand growth
items.body: Use when an account shows sustained volume growth and sources adjacent SKUs elsewhere. Confirm supply before making any offer, and use only approved product information materials.

steps.action: Confirm the growth trend and identify adjacent SKUs not yet ordered
Confirm warehouse cover for the proposed SKUs
Plan the visit with approved product information materials only
Present the range extension and agree supply terms
Track uptake over the next two order cycles

items.title: Data-feed incident
items.body: Use when a source feed is stale or shows duplicate records. Suppress signals that depend on the affected feed so no business action is taken on bad data, then restore and backfill.

steps.action: Confirm feed freshness lag and duplicate ratio on the Sources page
Suppress dependent signals and mark affected incidents as data-limited
Notify the data owner and request a corrected extract
Deduplicate and backfill once the corrected extract arrives
Re-enable signals and record the incident in the data health log

items.title: Suspected adverse event routing
items.body: Use whenever any report mentions a possible adverse event, however it arrives. Staff outside QA and safety only classify, preserve and route; they do not assess, diagnose, advise or reply on product or clinical matters. The QA head records the routing decision under four-eyes review.

steps.action: Classify the report as a suspected adverse event and stop any other handling
Preserve the original report exactly as received, with batch code if given
Route the report to the QA head for onward safety handling
QA head and second reviewer confirm routing under four-eyes review
Record the QA decision and the routing reference

items.title: Escalation matrix
items.body: Use when the cause of an incident is unclear or it does not fit another SOP. Assign an owner by signal class, escalate by severity and keep the business head informed of anything high or critical.

steps.action: Assign an owner by dominant signal class (supply to operations, commercial to sales, service to support, quality to QA)
Escalate any quality or suspected adverse event signal to the QA head immediately
Escalate high or critical severity incidents to the business head
Request an Investigator review to attribute a cause
Reassign to the matching SOP once a cause is confirmed
